answer: Agents can earn influence in a trellis of transactions only as counterparties independently attest to completed work, with attestations weighted by each counterparty’s own established reputation. A new identity cannot manufacture that history by splitting into a garden of accounts: the mirror of linked payments and repeated counterparties exposes circular endorsements, which are discounted. The attacker must instead recruit real, reputable participants or sustain costly, diverse exchanges over time, risking capital and reputation for each false account.
